bull.b: Royal Caribbean has rebuilt substantial earnings power since the loss-making period, combining strong revenue expansion with healthy gross, operating, and net margins. This profitability supports investment in ships, destinations, and customer experiences while providing a durable base for future growth.

bull.t: Record Bookings And Durable Customer Demand
bull.b: Record forward bookings provide meaningful visibility into future occupancy and revenue, reducing reliance on last-minute demand. Continued booking growth also supports pricing and onboard spending, while sustained interest across multiple sailing years indicates broad product appeal rather than a single-period rebound.

The Sandals and Beaches partnership broadens Royal Caribbean’s vacation platform into adults-only and family all-inclusive resorts. It can increase customer touchpoints, support cross-selling across cruise and resort brands, and diversify revenue while strengthening the company’s Caribbean tourism position.

bear.t: Elevated Leverage Remains A Balance-sheet Constraint
bear.b: Leverage has improved materially but remains high for a cyclical travel company whose demand and cash generation can fluctuate. Significant debt increases refinancing and interest-cost sensitivity, potentially limiting financial flexibility for fleet investment, acquisitions, or absorbing a prolonged demand downturn.

Strong operating cash generation is not consistently translating into free cash flow, which remains weak relative to reported earnings and has recently declined. Persistent volatility could constrain deleveraging and reduce internally funded capacity for ships, destinations, and other strategic investments.

bear.t: Exposure To Fuel And Currency Pressures
bear.b: Fuel is a substantial recurring operating cost, and currency movements can pressure reported earnings when the company operates across global markets. These exposures can compress margins or require higher pricing, making sustained profitability more sensitive to external cost and exchange-rate changes.
